title: Node capacity tags, health scoring, and routing playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for how platform should tag node capacity, compute a lightweight health score, and use that score in service discovery + routing decisions across regions. Focus is inference-serving clusters (GPU-heavy) but most ideas apply to CPU-only pools too.

Context / motivation:
- We need a single, compact representation of node capabilities so the control plane can make fast, deterministic routing decisions (prefetch routing table, fallbacks, cost-aware routing).
- Current inventory is fragmented: provisioning labels in infra, telemetry in a separate TSDB, and ephemeral health events in SRE tooling. This causes stale routing decisions and opaque failure modes.
- Goal: canonical node registry with static metadata + frequent health signals -> produce a 0-100 HealthScore per node and an up-to-date capacity view.

High-level components (control plane view):
1) Node agent (node-exporter-lite): collects local labels (from cloud metadata/CRI), GPU details (nvidia-smi output parsed), and health metrics; pushes to streaming telemetry (kafka/kinesis).
2) Inventory aggregator (region-local): subscribes to telemetry, merges with infra-provisioned labels from fleet registry, computes HealthScore, publishes to Inventory API and short-lived cache (redis).
3) Global inventory replicator: replicates aggregated node state across regions using CDC with monotonic sequence numbers (see replication notes).
4) Discovery API / Router: queryable service that returns candidate nodes or routing decisions given constraints (region, model family, min_gpu_mem, cost_tier) and auto-filters by HealthScore & capacity.
5) Reconciler: periodic job that detects label drift and triggers infra automation (e.g., mark for reprovision).

Node label schema (recommended canonical keys):
- region: <continent>-<region> (e.g. na-west, eu-central)
- zone: <zone-id> (e.g. na-west-1a)
- pool: <pool-name> (e.g. gpu-inference-highmem)
- instance_type: <cloud instance type> (e.g. p4d.24xlarge)
- capacity_cpu_cores: <int>
- capacity_memory_gb: <int>
- gpu.family: <nvidia|amd>
- gpu.model: <a100-40gb|a100-80gb|h100-80gb|t4>
- gpu.count: <int>
- gpu.memory_gb: <per-gpu int>
- gpu.compute_fp16_tflops: <int>  # optional, used for rough capacity comparison
- storage.class: <nvme|network-ssd|hdd>
- ephemeral_storage_gb: <int>
- network_gbps: <int>
- instance_age_days: <int>  # helpful for lifecycle policies
- criticality: <prod|staging|dev>
- cost_tier: <premium|standard|spot>  # drives fallback routing/cost trade-offs

Label conventions and rules:
- Keys must be lowercase, dot-separated namespaces allowed (gpu.*).
- gpu.model should be normalized to small set we use everywhere (mapping layer from cloud SKU to model token).
- Capacity values are integers and represent effective available resources at registration time (will be adjusted by aggregator).
- Avoid embedding ephemeral signals (like current_cpu_pct) into static labels. Those belong to health signals.

Health signals we ingest (streamed, time-windowed):
- heartbeat_ts: unix ms timestamp of last agent heartbeat
- cpu_util_pct_1m (avg 1m)
- mem_util_pct_1m
- gpu_util_pct_1m (per-node avg across gpus)
- gpu_temp_c_max (max across gpus)
- recent_ooms_1h (count)
- disk_error_rate_1h
- p95_inference_latency_ms (job-facing metric)
- serving_errors_5m (count of 5xx / infra errors)
- network_err_rate_1m
- offers_pending_queue_len (if node reports local queue/backlog)

HealthScore: compact 0-100 integer computed every 20s by aggregator.
- Rationale: keep coarse but meaningful for routing decisions and for quick fallbacks.
- Formula (proposal — tuned in ops):
  base = 100
  base -= 0.5 * cpu_util_pct_1m            // CPU pressure
  base -= 0.8 * mem_util_pct_1m            // memory pressure weighs more
  base -= 1.2 * gpu_util_pct_1m            // GPU load reduces headroom
  if gpu_temp_c_max > 85: base -= (gpu_temp_c_max - 85) * 0.8  // thermal risk
  base -= 15 * min(1, recent_ooms_1h / 3) // spike reduction for OOMs
  base -= 20 * sigmoid((p95_inference_latency_ms - target_p95)/target_p95)  // latency penalty
  base -= 30 * min(1, serving_errors_5m / 5)
  // clamp to 0..100 and round to int
- Example weights give quick downgrades when multiple signals fire. We keep the function deterministic and versioned.

Health categories (derived):
- HEALTHY: score >= 80
- DEGRADED: 50 <= score < 80
- UNSTABLE: 20 <= score < 50
- DRAIN: score < 20 OR explicit drain tag (used by SRE/automation)

Routing policy (discovery-side):
1) Request constraints: {region_preference, model_family, min_gpu_mem_gb, cost_tier_preference, latency_budget_ms}
2) Candidate selection pipeline:
   a) Region filter: if strict region_preference -> filter to region; else include cross-region candidates with penalty.
   b) Capability filter: match gpu.model/family and min_gpu_mem and instance capacity.
   c) Health filter: remove nodes with HealthScore < 20. Prefer HEALTHY nodes.
   d) Capacity scoring: compute score = alpha * HealthScore + beta * capacity_score + gamma * cost_score - delta * region_penalty - epsilon * estimated_queue_delay
   e) Return top N candidates or a single routing decision. If none match, fallback to lower-cost tiers or cross-region depending on policy (see fallback rules).

Capacity scoring details:
- capacity_score is a normalized field derived from (free_gpu_slots * per_gpu_mem + free_cpu) scaled to 0..100. The aggregator computes free_gpu_slots by observing current allocations in the local scheduler and combining with capacity labels.
- cost_score maps cost_tier to 0..100 (premium=90, standard=60, spot=20).
- region_penalty: 0 for same region, 20 for same continent, 40 for cross-continent. Tunable per customer/route.

Fallback rules (prioritized):
- Try same region, degrade to same continent, then cross-continent.
- If HealthScore severe (<30) but capability matches and latency budget allows, consider for non-critical traffic only (traffic shaping label).
- If nothing available, return an expanded candidate set and signal client to do retry-with-backoff. Router should include reason codes (EXACT_MATCH, COST_FALLBACK, REGION_FALLBACK, HEALTH_FALLBACK).

Multi-region replication and consistency:
- Inventories are region-local for low-latency reads; global replicator publishes a summarized view to other regions every 15s.
- Use monotonic sequence numbers per node record. Updates carry seq_num + last_modified_ts.
- Conflict resolution: last-writer-wins using seq_num then timestamp. Avoid complex vector clocks unless needed — we prefer monotonic update counters from region aggregator.
- Staleness window: consumers should consider records fresh if last_modified_ts within 40s (configurable). Use HealthScore decay to 0 after 90s without heartbeat.

APIs (examples):
- GET /inventory/v1/nodes?region=na-west&gpu_model=a100-40gb&min_gpu_mem=40 -> list of node summaries (node_id, labels, health_score, free_gpu_slots, seq_num, last_modified)
- POST /inventory/v1/query-route {constraints...} -> routing decision {node_id, reason_code, expires_at}

Sample inventory node summary (presented as example, actual API is JSON):
{
  "node_id": "node-az1-1234",
  "labels": "region=na-west,zone=na-west-1a,pool=gpu-inference-highmem,gpu.model=a100-40gb,gpu.count=8,gpu.memory_gb=40,cost_tier=premium",
  "health_score": "87",
  "free_gpu_slots": "3",
  "seq_num": "9765",
  "last_modified": "2025-02-03T14:12:09Z"
}

Telemetry and sampling considerations:
- Not all signals need to be streamed at full fidelity. Use 20s aggregates for health-critical signals (cpu/gpu util) and 1m for latency.
- Keep the node->aggregator payload small (<=1KB) to support millions of nodes in the future.
- Scrub PII and customer identifiers at the agent before sending to telemetry pipeline.

Operational playbook (quick):
- If HealthScore drop detected across many nodes in region: check agent heartbeat and ingestion pipeline (kafka partitioning).
- Frequent sequence_num regressions indicate aggregator restarts or clock issues — escalate to infra-runbooks.
- If routing returns no candidates: fall back to pre-baked model-hosting pools (global).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include per-GPU hotplug info (e.g. MIG partitions) in canonical labels? (pros: precise scheduling; cons: label explosion).
- How to expose per-customer isolation constraints in the scoring model (tenancy, hw-accelerators)?
- Policy: aggressive draining threshold for thermal events vs. latency-driven thresholds — Ops to simulate with synthetic load.
- Benchmarks: run replay test with 10k nodes to validate 20s scoring cadence.

References / links:
- Related design: confluence: inventory-design-v2
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1243
- Jira epic for rollout: PLAT-812

Notes-to-self:
- Keep scoring code in a single module and version it. Any change must be flagged and testable via replay harness.
- Prioritize small, stable set of labels; mapping layer can expand cloud SKUs to canonical tokens.

End of draft.
